Which statement and reason about these hydrides is correct?

options.A: The boiling point of PH₃ is much lower than the boiling point of H₂O because PH₃ does not form hydrogen bonds or instantaneous dipole-induced dipole forces between its molecules.
options.B: The boiling point of HF is higher than the boiling point of HCl because the bond energy of H–F is greater than the bond energy of H–Cl.
options.C: The boiling point of H₂O is higher than the boiling point of HF because each hydrogen bond between the H₂O molecules is stronger than each hydrogen bond between HF molecules.
options.D: The boiling points of PH₃ and HCl are similar because the molecules of PH₃ and HCl have the same number of electrons and similar intermolecular forces.

Nitrogen, N₂, and carbon monoxide, CO, both have Mr = 28.
The boiling point of N₂ is 77K.
The boiling point of CO is 82K.
What could be responsible for this difference in boiling points?
CO molecules have a permanent dipole; the N₂ molecules are not polar.

options.A: N₂ has and bonding; CO has bonding only.
options.B: N₂ has a strong NŁN bond; CO has a C=O bond.
options.C: The CO molecule has more electrons than the N₂ molecule.
